These continuing returns remain materially above the required return and therefore grant a durable franchise; they are not observed perpetual returns.

In the base, last explicit FCFF of 229.21 billion becomes 231.53 billion in the terminal year, a +1.01% change. Changing terminal reinvestment alone to continue forecast sales-to-capital raises value to $164.55. The handoff is visible rather than a hidden cash cliff. Terminal value still supplies 55.2% of enterprise value; long-duration cash assumptions deserve at least as much attention as a quarter’s margin.

Capital-efficiency uncertainty is also quantified. Changing only explicit-forecast sales-to-capital from 1x to 6x gives $152.03 to $164.58. Setting only explicit-forecast net investment to zero gives $167.09, with terminal reinvestment retained; this is an unachievable-investment illustration, not a floor. Setting only the return on new terminal investment equal to WACC lowers value to $139.85.","fix":"State why 50% terminal ROIC is the preferred base despite no primary observed ROIC support, or lower it / rebalance scenarios. Revenue would reach $2.21 trillion in FY2036, versus $0.82 trillion in base; the final annual increase would be $313.28 billion. For scale, FY2026 added $62.673 billion and the base decade compounds at approximately 5.5%.

This is an aggregate requirement check, not a category-level adoption forecast. It holds the materialized margin path rather than rebuilding Products/Services mix and expense amounts; it cannot simultaneously be read as the original operating build. The $2.21 trillion outcome would require an evidenced combination of device pricing/volume, retained Services economics and new monetization at a scale not established by the present packet.
